title: Integral models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and the separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. All schemes below are Noetherian schemes in this setting. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\cO_E$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, and residue field $\kappa_E=\cO_E/\pi_E$. Fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Write $C_X=(\cO_E)_X$ for the constant coefficient sheaf and $R_X=\cO_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\cO_E}\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ for the completed coefficient sheaf [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Write $D_R(X)=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},R_X)$ and $D_C(X)=D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},C_X)$ for the derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The categories $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ mean bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and their full subcategory of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]; derived completeness means that the canonical map to the derived limit of the reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$ is an isomorphism [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. For constant coefficients use the same condition with $C_X$.

Let $\Dc(X,\cO_E)\subset D_C(X)$ consist of derived $\pi_E$-complete complexes $L$ for which $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{C_X}(\kappa_E)_X$ has constructible cohomology pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and finite Tor dimension. This is the constant-coefficient category of [det-lem-integral-models-stacks]. Then $\Dctf(X,\cO_E)=\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and the following hold.

1. Restriction of scalars along $C_X\to R_X$ gives an equivalence between the derived $\pi_E$-complete objects of $D_R(X)$ and those of $D_C(X)$.
2. For $K\in D_R(X)$, $K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ if and only if $\operatorname{Res}K\in\Dc(X,\cO_E)$. Equivalently, $K$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ precisely when it is derived complete and $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}(\kappa_E)_X$ is a bounded constructible complex pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$.
3. The categories $\Dbc(-,\cO_E)$ are preserved by the inverse image $f^*$ for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in the setting, by $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}-$, and by $a_!=i_*u_!$ for every locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow X$, with $u$ open and $i$ closed. The inverse image and tensor functors are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; open extension by zero is [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].
4. Every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained by finitely many cones and shifts from objects $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$, where $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally closed and $L_0$ is a lisse finite free $\cO_{E,S}$-module, meaning a module pro-étale locally isomorphic to a finite free coefficient module. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is obtained in the same way from objects $\QbarX\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ for one finite subextension $E\subset\Qlb$ depending on the object; here $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$ uses [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Moreover $a_!L_0\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and for every $n\ge1$ its derived reduction is $a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$, a bounded constructible complex with coefficients $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$.

proof.text: Apply localizingClosure_ctf_equals_bc to the integral coefficient object, with the reflexive coefficient isomorphism. Its integral finite-Tor equality is the opening equality.

Apply the embedded completion comparison to obtain the required complete-subcategory equivalence and the pointwise completeness iff. This is clause (1). Its proof retains the flat common-quotient tower and normalized derived-limit/unit argument of the unit.

For each K the embedded Stacks criterion is the first iff. Compose it with and_congr of the reversed completeness iff and the residue comparison to obtain the second iff in clause (2). The residue comparison retains the constant-field Tor criterion and constructible etale comparison.

Apply integralModelsOperations for inverse-image preservation. Exactness of the inverse image identifies its total left derived functor with mapDerivedCategory; transport constructibility along leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory using the proved repleteness statement.
The tensor and locally closed extension-by-zero assertions are exactly clauses (2) and (3) of integralModelsOperations, with the given schemes and morphisms.

Apply the three assertions of integral_models_generators: finite cones and shifts over E, one finite intermediate field for each algebraic-closure object, and integral constructibility with every positive derived reduction for the same locally free lattice.

blueprint_update.statement:
For integral coefficients $\Dctf(X,\cO_E)=\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$: the finite constant local models have
finite projective dimension over the discrete valuation ring. By
[sk-prop-integral-criterion], an object lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ precisely when it is derived
complete and its reduction modulo $\pi_E$ is a bounded constructible complex pulled back from
$X_{\mathrm{ét}}$. The Stacks Project works with the category $\Dc(X,\cO_E)$ of \stacks{09C1},
built from modules over the constant sheaf $\cO_E$ instead of $\cO_{E,X}$. The next lemma
identifies the two, so that the results of the Stacks Project apply. Combined with lattices,
it also shows that the rational categories are generated by scalar extensions of integral
objects with classical torsion reductions.

1. Restriction of scalars along the map from the constant sheaf $\cO_E$ to $\cO_{E,X}$ is an
   equivalence between the derived complete objects of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ and the
   derived complete complexes of modules over the constant sheaf $\cO_E$.
2. An object $K$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ if and only if its
   restriction of scalars lies in $\Dc(X,\cO_E)$.
3. $\Dbc(-,\cO_E)$ is preserved by
   $f^*\colon D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ for every morphism
   $f\colon X\to Y$, by $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}$ on $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$, and by
   $a_!\colon D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ for every locally closed
   immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$.
4. Every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained by finitely many cones and shifts from objects
   $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$, where $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is a locally closed immersion and $L_0$
   is a lisse finite free $\cO_{E,S}$-module. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is obtained in the
   same way from the objects $\QbarX\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$, for some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.
   The reductions of $a_!L_0$ modulo $\pi_E^n$ are bounded constructible complexes on
   $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with coefficients in $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$.

proof.text:
(1) and (2). The map from the constant sheaf $\cO_E$ to $\cO_{E,X}$ is flat and induces
isomorphisms modulo every $\pi_E^n$ (\stacks{099L}). Hence restriction of scalars is an
equivalence on derived complete objects, by \stacks{099I}; this is (1)
([det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients]). By \stacks{09C1}, an object of
$\Dc(X,\cO_E)$ is a derived complete complex whose reduction modulo $\pi_E$ is constructible of
finite Tor dimension over $\cO_E/\pi_E$. Since $\cO_E/\pi_E$ is a field, every bounded complex
has finite Tor dimension over it, so this is the description of $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ in
[sk-prop-integral-criterion]; together with (1) this gives (2). Details:
[det-lem-integral-models-stacks].

(3) By [sk-prop-integral-criterion], an object of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ lies in
$\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ if and only if it is derived complete with constructible reduction modulo
$\pi_E$ (condition (2)), and if and only if it admits a finite stratification such that on each
stratum $S$, pro-étale locally, $K|_S\simeq\cO_{E,S}\otimes_{\cO_E}P^\bullet$ for a bounded
complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $\cO_E$-modules (condition (3)). The implication from (2) to
(3) is [sk-prop-integral-local-structure]. For each of the three operations we check one of
these two conditions.

*Inverse image.* By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], $f^*$ sends finite free
$\cO_{E,Y}$-modules to finite free $\cO_{E,X}$-modules, so the local description is preserved.

*Extension by zero.* The functor $a_!=i_*u_!$ preserves derived completeness: $u_!$ for a
quasi-compact open immersion $u$ preserves limits by \stacks{09BP}, and $i_*$ is exact and
preserves limits by \stacks{09AA} and \stacks{09BM}. Both functors commute with reduction
modulo $\pi_E$ and preserve constructibility of the reductions.

*Tensor product.* Let $K,M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and choose a stratification for $K$ as above.
Derived completeness and constructibility of the reduction modulo $\pi_E$ are both preserved
by cones, so $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ is closed under cones. The localization triangles along the
strata exhibit $K$ as a finite iterated extension of the objects $a_!a^*K$, for the strata
$a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$, and $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$ preserves these triangles. Hence it
suffices to show that $(a_!a^*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$. For this we use
the projection formula for a locally closed immersion: for $L\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$
and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ the canonical map
$$
(a_!L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\longrightarrow a_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M)
$$
is an isomorphism. To see this, write $a=i\circ u$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed, so that
$a_!=i_*u_!$. On $S$ the map restricts to the identity of $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M$, and on
every complementary stratum both sides restrict to zero. Restriction to the strata is exact,
and these restrictions are jointly conservative by \stacks{09AD}. By the parts on inverse image
and extension by zero, it therefore remains to see that $a^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M$ lies in
$\Dbc(S,\cO_E)$. Since $a^*K$ is pro-étale locally a bounded complex of finite free modules,
tensoring with it preserves derived completeness. The reduction modulo $\pi_E$ of the tensor
product is the tensor product of the reductions, which is constructible. Details:
[det-lem-integral-models-operations]; compare the preservation statements of
[sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors].

(4) For $\Qlb$, first descend to a finite $E$ by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]. By
[sk-cor-coefficient-heart-ii], every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained by finitely many cones
and shifts from sheaves $a_!L$ with $L$ lisse. By [sk-lem-stratified-lattice], after refining
the stratum $S$ by a finite stratification (which replaces $a_!L$ by finitely many extensions
of such sheaves), $L$ contains a lattice $L_0$ with $L_0[1/\ell]=L$, so
$a_!L=(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$. The reduction of $L_0$ modulo $\pi_E^n$ is a locally constant sheaf of
finitely presented $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$-modules, so it comes from the étale site by \stacks{099Y}.
